label: copy-phase input r (re-fed letter r)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the input token is the letter r during the copy phase (i.e., the model has just output r and it is fed back). Never fires in the original phase (including on original r) or on <DEL>. Recall ~1.0; precision ~0.86, with false positives concentrated on late copy positions (recall_idx >= 5) where r is often silent. Magnitude is largest when r is re-fed early in the copy (recall_idx 1-3, i.e., r was original token 1-3) and decays at later positions; in r r runs the first copy-phase r is strongest and the second weaker. Does not depend on which token is being output next.

issues: The claims hold up. On test, (phase==2)&(in_tok==r) gets P 0.864, R 0.9999, F1 0.927, mass recall 1.0. There are only 9 missed active steps, holding 0.0% of the activation mass: weak f/d/x activations just before an r at step 11.

On dev the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phase (0 of 3.2M original steps, including original r) and is never active on <DEL>. All activation mass falls in the copy phase, on in_tok=r.

The false positives are real but come from the activation fading, not from a separable subclass. Re-fed r at recall_idx>=5 fires only about 60% of the time (test P 0.62), versus roughly 95% at t<=12. Within recall_idx>=5, precision stays at 0.56-0.70 when split by to_go, L, n_digits, prev_tok type (digit, letter, vowel), in_count or next_out. No predicate isolates the silent cases.

Magnitude peaks at recall_idx 2-3: recall_idx 2 has 38.6% of the mass at about the same firing rate as recall_idx 1 and 4, and later positions are weaker. This is consistent with the claim. The top examples are all 'x r r' runs where the first copy-phase r is near 1.0 and the second is 0.4-0.7, which supports the claim that the first r in a run is stronger.
next_out has a flat profile (lift about 1.8x for every value), which supports the claim that the next output token does not matter.
Small overclaim: the label says 'copy-phase input r', but a copy-phase r at late positions is silent about 40% of the time. The explanation already says this.
